explanation: Shopify cannot see the DNS records that should point your domain at the store. Until they verify, SSL will not issue and checkout on that domain can fail.
steps: Online Store → Domains and click the domain that shows an error.
If Shopify hosts the domain, click Verify connection and wait up to 24 hours.
If a third party hosts it, set the A record to 23.227.38.65 and the www CNAME to shops.myshopify.com.
Remove old AAAA or conflicting CNAME records. Extra records are the usual reason verification stalls.
Once Connected, set it as the primary domain so SSL can finish issuing.

explanation: A Liquid or JSON template error is blocking the editor or the live storefront. Shopify usually names the file in the banner.
steps: Online Store → Themes → the red error count. Click it to open the first broken file.
Read the line number. Typical causes: a missing {% endif %}, a deleted section still referenced in JSON, or a typo in a filter.
If you cannot fix it quickly, Actions → Duplicate the live theme, then roll back the broken file from older versions (each file has a version history).
Disable recently installed theme-app extensions if the error appeared after an app install.
Preview the theme on a product, collection, and cart page before publishing again.

explanation: Taxes only calculate when a registration exists for that region and the product is not marked tax-exempt.
steps: Settings → Taxes and duties.
Add a tax registration for every region where you have nexus or a VAT number.
Open a product and confirm Charge tax is enabled unless it is legally exempt.
If you use Shopify Tax, let it manage rates. Manual overrides on a country will fight it.
Test checkout with an address in that region and compare the tax line to your registration.

explanation: Checkout behavior is controlled in Settings → Checkout, not in the theme. Theme edits will not change account requirements or tipping.
steps: Settings → Checkout.
Customer accounts: choose Optional unless you truly need a login — requiring accounts increases abandonment.
Tipping, email marketing opt-in, and form fields are on this same page.
Checkout language / editor is under Settings → Checkout → Customize.
After changes, test in an incognito window so a logged-in staff session does not hide the real flow.

match_phrases: continue selling when out of stock
synonyms: sold out but I have stock
explanation: The product is hidden from purchase because inventory tracking hit zero, the variant is not published, or stock sits at a location that does not fulfill online.
steps: Open the product → Variants → Inventory. Add stock to a location that fulfills online orders.
If you want preorders, check Continue selling when out of stock.
Confirm the product is available on the Online Store sales channel.
A draft or archived product will not appear on the storefront even with stock.
If only one variant fails, check that variant's inventory — not the parent product.

explanation: Two apps injecting into the same cart, checkout, or product page is one of the most common "mystery" breakages.
steps: List apps installed in the last 7 days. Those are the first suspects.
Disable theme app embeds: Online Store → Themes → Customize → App embeds.
If checkout broke, disable checkout and thank-you extensions under Settings → Checkout → Customize.
Retest after each change. When the store recovers, leave that app off and contact its support.
Avoid two apps that both do reviews, upsells, or shipping — pick one.

explanation: The storefront is still behind Shopify's password page. That is not a DNS or theme bug.
steps: Online Store → Preferences (or Themes → the password banner).
Uncheck Restrict access to visitors with the password.
Save. Open the store URL in an incognito window to confirm the real homepage loads.
If you still see a coming-soon page, that is a theme template — publish your live theme.
Search engines will not index a password-protected store.

explanation: Staff accounts only see what the store owner granted. Payments, billing, and domains are often hidden on purpose.
steps: The store owner goes to Settings → Users and permissions.
Open the staff member and enable the missing permissions (Settings, Finances, Apps, etc.).
If 2FA is required and the staff member lost their device, the owner can reset two-step authentication there.
Collaborator accounts requested from an agency need the owner to approve a collaborator request email.
Owners who are locked out must use Shopify's account recovery — staff cannot reset the owner.

explanation: Shopify notification emails fail or land in spam when the sender domain is not authenticated, or the notification was disabled.
steps: Settings → Notifications and confirm Order confirmation is enabled.
Settings → Notifications → Sender email: add your domain and complete SPF/DKIM as shown.
Do not send from a free Gmail/Yahoo address — providers block it.
Check the customer's spam folder and the order timeline to see if Shopify sent the mail.
Branded domains need a CNAME Shopify gives you; add it at your DNS host and click Verify.

explanation: A Market controls whether a country can see the store, which catalog/prices they get, and which domain they land on.
steps: Settings → Markets and open the country that is failing.
The market must be Active / published. A draft market hides the storefront for that country.
Check the catalog assigned to the market — an empty catalog makes every product appear unavailable.
Domains and languages for that market are on the same page.
Use the market preview (globe icon) rather than a VPN when testing.

explanation: Checkout is sandboxed. Old theme pixels will not see purchases — they must be installed as customer events pixels.
steps: Settings → Customer events.
Add the Meta, Google, or custom pixel there — not as a script tag in theme.liquid.
Grant the pixel permission to connect to marketing and sales data.
Use the pixel helper (Meta) or GA4 DebugView and run a test checkout.
Remove duplicate pixels from the theme to avoid double-counted purchases.

explanation: Gift cards are a special product type. They must be issued, not just created as a normal product with a price.
steps: Products → Gift cards (or add a new product of type Gift card).
Do not require shipping on gift cards.
To issue one manually: Orders → the order → or Products → Gift cards → Issue gift card.
Customers apply the code at checkout. Staff can also apply it on a draft order.
Check the gift card's remaining balance if a customer says it did not work.

cause: Footer icons come from Theme settings → Social media. A handle like @mystore will not work — paste the full https URL.
explanation: This is a theme setting, not a sales channel. Pinterest and Google profile links go in the same list as Instagram and Facebook.
steps: Online Store → Themes → Customize on your live theme.
Open Theme settings (the paintbrush / gear at the bottom left) → Social media.
Paste the full profile URL, for example https://www.pinterest.com/yourshop or your Google Business Profile link. Not just the name.
Open the Footer section and turn on Show social media icons / Brand information if the icons are still missing.
Save, then open the store in a new tab and tap the icon to confirm it opens the right profile.
target_ui_hint: Online Store > Themes > Customize > Social media

cause: The Google & YouTube channel only lists Google accounts where you are an Admin. An unverified Business Profile or the wrong Google login will look like a broken link.
explanation: This is Sales channels → Google & YouTube, not the theme social-icon field.
steps: In Shopify admin search, type Google and open Google & YouTube. Install it from the App Store if it is missing.
Click Connect Google Account and pick the same Google login that owns Merchant Center / the Business Profile.
If Merchant Center is missing from the list, open Merchant Center → Settings → Account access and add that Google email as Admin.
A Business Profile must already be verified in Google before Shopify can connect it. Finish Google’s postcard / email / phone verify first.
Staff need Apps and channels + Manage settings permission. If Connect is greyed out, have the store owner do this step.

cause: Pinterest only links one Business account per store. A personal Pinterest login, a changed password, or a leftover old install will stall on a blank page.
explanation: Use the official Pinterest app / sales channel. Theme social icons only add a footer link — they do not sync products.
steps: You need a Pinterest Business account (not a personal one) and the store password page turned off.
Settings → Apps and sales channels → Shopify App Store → install Pinterest.
Open the Pinterest channel → Connect Pinterest account. Log in as the Business account owner.
If you get a blank page or a stuck green bar: on Pinterest go to Settings → Security and login → revoke Shopify, then connect again from Shopify.
To switch Business accounts, uninstall Pinterest in Settings → Apps and sales channels, then install and connect the new account. Only one Pinterest Business profile can be linked at a time.
target_ui_hint: Settings > Apps and sales channels > Pinterest

cause: Shopify Collective is two apps, not a theme setting. Retailers import products. Suppliers share a price list and fulfill the order.
explanation: Look under Sales channels for Collective: Retailer or Collective: Supplier. If neither is there, install from the App Store. Pause and Build plans cannot use it.
steps: Decide your role: Retailer = sell someone else’s products with no inventory. Supplier = let other stores sell yours and you ship.
In admin search type Collective. Open Collective: Retailer or Collective: Supplier. If missing: Settings → Apps and sales channels → Shopify App Store → Shopify Collective.
Install, then open Sales channels → that Collective app and finish the checklist (country, currency, paid plan, Shopify Payments).
Retailer: invite a supplier or use Discovery, then Import products. Supplier: create a price list, set it Active, invite a retailer by email.
If it says not eligible: Sales channels → Collective: Supplier → Settings and fix the red checklist. Both stores must be in a supported country and the same currency.

match_phrases: how to get to edit code
synonyms: how do I edit my theme
cause: Customize (Edit theme) is the visual editor. Edit code is a different button behind the ⋯ menu. They are not the same screen.
explanation: Use Customize for colors, sections, Custom Liquid, and social links. Use Edit code only when a guide says to open theme.liquid or a .liquid file.
steps: Online Store → Themes. Your live theme is the one marked Current.
To change look and sections: click Customize (some phones say Edit theme). That is the safe editor. Save there.
To open files: on that same theme click ⋯ (three dots) next to Customize → Edit code. Do not click Customize for this.
Always ⋯ → Duplicate the live theme first. Edit the copy, Preview, then Publish only when it looks right.
Staff who cannot see Edit code need Themes permission from the store owner (Settings → Users and permissions).
target_ui_hint: Online Store > Themes > Customize or ⋯ Edit code

cause: Most app snippets belong in a Custom Liquid section in Customize — not in Edit code. That keeps the theme upgradable.
explanation: Custom Liquid is a block you add in the visual editor. It is the first place to paste Liquid an app gives you.
steps: Online Store → Themes → Customize on the live theme.
Open the page (Home, Product, or Footer) where the snippet should show.
Add section or Add block → Custom Liquid (sometimes named Custom HTML / Liquid).
Paste the snippet, then Save. Preview the page on phone and desktop.
If Custom Liquid is not in the list, your theme is old — use ⋯ → Edit code only as a last step, on a duplicated theme.
target_ui_hint: Online Store > Themes > Customize > Custom Liquid

cause: The <head> lives in layout/theme.liquid. Tracking pixels should not go there — checkout will not see them.
explanation: Tracking (Meta, GA4, TikTok) → Settings → Customer events. Only paste into <head> when the instructions say theme.liquid and it is not a purchase pixel.
steps: If this is a pixel / conversion tag: Settings → Customer events → Add custom pixel. Stop here.
Otherwise: Online Store → Themes → ⋯ next to the theme → Duplicate, then ⋯ → Edit code on the copy.
Left sidebar → layout → theme.liquid.
Find </head>. Paste the snippet on a new line just above </head>. Do not delete {{ content_for_header }}.
Save, Preview the unpublished theme, then Publish only if the store still loads.
target_ui_hint: Online Store > Themes > ⋯ > Edit code > layout/theme.liquid

synonyms: add privacy policy to my store
checkout policy link missing on store
cause: Do not copy the policy into theme.liquid. Save it under Settings → Policies, then link that Shopify page in the footer menu.
explanation: Settings → Policies hosts the real privacy policy at /policies/privacy-policy. Checkout already links it. The storefront theme only needs a footer (or menu) link — not pasted HTML in Edit code.
steps: Settings → Policies (Written policies). Open Privacy policy.
Insert template or paste your lawyer/generator text. Review it. Save. Shopify now hosts https://your-store.com/policies/privacy-policy and links it in checkout.
Do not open Edit code / theme.liquid and paste the policy. That duplicates it and breaks updates.
Content → Menus (older admin: Online Store → Navigation) → Footer menu → Add menu item.
Name: Privacy policy. In Link, search Policies and pick Privacy policy (or paste /policies/privacy-policy). Add → Save menu.
Optional: Online Store → Themes → Customize → Footer. If the theme has Show policy links, turn it on.
Open the storefront, scroll to the footer, tap Privacy policy. You should land on /policies/privacy-policy, not a blank Page.
target_ui_hint: Settings > Policies, then Content > Menus > Footer

synonyms: I edited the theme nothing happened
cause: You edited a draft, the wrong theme, or the browser is showing an old copy.
explanation: Shopify only shows the Published theme. Customize must be on that theme, then Save. Hard-refresh the storefront.
steps: Stop. Do not tap Edit code or paste Liquid yet. Online Store → Themes → ⋯ → Duplicate first. A bad paste can take the storefront down.
Online Store → Themes. Confirm the theme you edited has the Published badge — not a duplicate or trial.
Click Customize on the Published theme. Make the change again. Tap Save (top right).
On the storefront: hard-refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R or Cmd+Shift+R). Try an incognito window.
If you used Preview, that link is not the live shop. Click Publish only when Preview looks right.

cause: A section is hidden or stacked wrong on mobile. Fix it in Customize, not in CSS files.
explanation: Theme editor has a mobile preview. Hide/show and padding per section there.
steps: Stop. Do not tap Edit code or paste Liquid yet. Online Store → Themes → ⋯ → Duplicate first. A bad paste can take the storefront down.
Online Store → Themes → Customize on the Published theme.
Bottom of the editor: switch to the phone preview icon.
Click the broken section. Check Hide on mobile, image height, and padding. Save.
If an app section is the problem: Theme settings → App embeds → turn that embed off, Save, recheck mobile.
target_ui_hint: Online Store > Themes > Customize > mobile preview

cause: A Shopify or theme update changed a section. Roll back or duplicate, don’t patch live Liquid first.
steps: Stop. Do not tap Edit code or paste Liquid yet. Online Store → Themes → ⋯ → Duplicate first. A bad paste can take the storefront down.
Online Store → Themes. If Shopify added an update card, open it and read which files changed.
⋯ on the Published theme → Duplicate (safety copy).
⋯ → Last saved or older library version if you need yesterday’s theme.
Apps → remove or update any theme-app extension installed the same day.
Preview a product, collection, cart, and checkout before you Publish again.

cause: Uninstalling an app often leaves an embed or a snippet. That leftover can break a section or slow the shop.
steps: Stop. Do not tap Edit code or paste Liquid yet. Online Store → Themes → ⋯ → Duplicate first. A bad paste can take the storefront down.
Settings → Apps and sales channels. Confirm the app is uninstalled.
Online Store → Themes → Customize → App embeds. Turn off anything named after the old app. Save.
Customize → look for leftover app blocks in header, footer, product. Remove the block, don’t Edit code.
If a step from the app’s docs says “paste in theme.liquid”: ignore it on the live theme. Duplicate first, or skip — most modern apps use embeds.

cause: Several apps inject scripts. Two pop-ups or two review widgets often collide.
steps: Settings → Apps and sales channels. List every app that touches the storefront (pop-up, reviews, upsell, chat).
Online Store → Themes → Customize → App embeds. Turn off all but one suspect. Save. Check the storefront.
Turn embeds back on one at a time until the break returns. Uninstall or replace that app.
Never stack two apps that do the same job (two pop-ups, two reviews).

cause: Huge images, extra apps, and extra pixels delay the page. Fix those before editing theme code.
steps: Stop. Do not tap Edit code or paste Liquid yet. Online Store → Themes → ⋯ → Duplicate first. A bad paste can take the storefront down.
Online Store → Themes → Customize → Theme settings → Media / images. Use Shopify-hosted images; don’t upload 4000px photos.
Settings → Customer events. Remove pixels you don’t use. Each pixel adds wait time.
Customize → App embeds: turn off unused embeds (especially sliders, pop-ups, live chat on every page).
Online Store → Preferences → check password is off if you meant the shop to be public (password pages also feel “slow”).
target_ui_hint: Theme settings > images, then Customer events

cause: Inventory is tracking at the wrong location, or a channel isn’t using Continue selling.
steps: Settings → Locations. Confirm which location should fulfill online orders.
Products → Inventory. Filter the product. Check On hand vs Available at each location.
Product page → Inventory: Track quantity is on. Continue selling when out of stock is off if you don’t want oversell.
Sales channels: if Amazon/eBay/POS also sell, wait a few minutes after a stock edit — sync is not instant.
Orders → the oversold order → fulfill from the location that still has stock, or refund.

cause: A bulk inventory edit sent a blank or negative quantity, or the variant no longer exists.
steps: Don’t retry the same CSV. Open Products → Inventory and fix one product by hand first.
Export a fresh CSV from Shopify (not an old file). Quantity must be a number, never blank.
If you deleted a variant, remove that row from the CSV.
Bulk editor: change fewer than 50 variants at a time if saves fail.

cause: Additional scripts or old checkout CSS can hide Pay now. Shopify Plus checkout extra scripts are the usual suspect; on basic plans, an app or discount is more likely.
steps: Stop. Do not tap Edit code or paste Liquid yet. Online Store → Themes → ⋯ → Duplicate first. A bad paste can take the storefront down.
Try checkout in an incognito window with no apps. If it works, an app is involved.
Settings → Checkout. Note any additional scripts. Temporarily clear them on a duplicate theme / after copying the text somewhere safe.
Customize → App embeds: turn off upsell, trust-badge, and checkout-related apps. Retest.
Discounts: disable automatic discounts, retry, then add back one at a time.

cause: The code has a date, usage, or combination rule — or two automatics are blocking each other.
steps: Discounts → open the code. Check status Active, start/end dates, and minimum purchase.
Combinations: if it can’t combine with product discounts, turn the other automatic off to test.
Customer eligibility: if it’s “specific customers”, your test account must be on that list.
Abandoned checkout emails: Settings → Notifications → Abandoned checkout. Must be enabled. Customer must have entered an email at checkout.

cause: Filtered collection URLs look like extra pages to Google. Fix in collection + search settings, not in theme.liquid.
steps: Stop. Do not tap Edit code or paste Liquid yet. Online Store → Themes → ⋯ → Duplicate first. A bad paste can take the storefront down.
Products → Collections → the collection → Search engine listing preview. Write a unique title and description.
Online Store → Navigation. Fix breadcrumbs by using one menu parent, not duplicate collection links.
If you use filter apps, in that app turn off “index filter pages” or similar. Don’t paste robots.txt by hand unless you already have a duplicate theme.
Google Search Console: request indexing only for the main collection URL, not every ?filter= link.

cause: Shopify caps variants at 100 per product. Images look blurry when the file is small or the theme stretches it.
steps: Products → the product. If you need more than 100 variants, split into two products (e.g. by color) instead of Edit code hacks.
Media: upload PNG/JPG at least 2048px on the long side. Don’t screenshot a photo.
Click a variant → choose its image so the gallery matches the option.
Customize → product page → image block: check crop (circle/portrait) isn’t crushing the photo.
Stop. Do not tap Edit code or paste Liquid yet. Online Store → Themes → ⋯ → Duplicate first. A bad paste can take the storefront down.

cause: Markets must include the country and a price list. The language selector is a theme setting, not a Liquid snippet you paste.
steps: Settings → Markets. Open the country. Status must be Active. A price list or Shopify Payments currency must exist.
Settings → Payments → Shopify Payments → currencies (if you use Shopify Payments).
Online Store → Themes → Customize → header. Add the markets / language selector block if the theme has one. Do not paste a random language switcher into theme.liquid.
Stop. Do not tap Edit code or paste Liquid yet. Online Store → Themes → ⋯ → Duplicate first. A bad paste can take the storefront down.
Test in incognito with a VPN only as a last check — Shopify uses the market you pick more than IP.

cause: Tax is a Markets + Taxes setting. Carrier/3PL errors are usually the app connection, not Liquid.
steps: Settings → Taxes and duties. Collect tax is on. Open the country and check overrides.
Settings → Markets → the country → duties and import taxes if you sell internationally.
Settings → Shipping and delivery → carrier: reconnect if rates are zero.
3PL apps: Settings → Apps → the 3PL → reconnect. Then Orders → fulfill a test order.
Don’t paste tax tables into the theme.

cause: The refund policy lives in Settings → Policies. The website only shows it if the footer (or a menu) links that Shopify page — not if you paste it into the theme.
explanation: Settings → Policies hosts /policies/refund-policy. Checkout already links it. Add the same link in the footer menu so shoppers see it on the site.
steps: Settings → Policies. Open Refund policy (also Shipping policy and Terms of service if you need those).
Insert template or paste your text. Save. Shopify now hosts https://your-store.com/policies/refund-policy.
Do not paste the policy into Edit code / theme.liquid.
Content → Menus → Footer menu → Add menu item. Name: Refund policy. In Link, search Policies and pick Refund policy (or /policies/refund-policy). Save.
Optional: Online Store → Themes → Customize → Footer → turn on Show policy links if the theme has it.
Open the live shop, footer, tap Refund policy. You should land on /policies/refund-policy.
target_ui_hint: Settings > Policies, then Content > Menus > Footer

match_phrases: line of text across all products
add a line of text to all products
how do I add a line of text across all products
cause: One block on the product template shows on every product. Do not paste the line into hundreds of descriptions, and do not let Sidekick bulk-edit descriptions for this.
explanation: Online Store → Themes → Customize → Products template → add a Rich text block. That one block is the line on all products that use that template.
steps: Decide: all product pages only (do this), or a bar on every page of the shop (that is the announcement bar, not this).
Online Store → Themes → ⋯ → Duplicate the live theme. Do not Edit code on the published theme.
Customize the copy. Top bar: Products → Default product.
Add block → Rich text (or Heading). Type the one line. Drag it under the title or price. Save.
If some products use another template: Products → [product] → Theme template. Add the same block on that template too, or switch them to Default product.
Preview a few products. Publish the copy only when the line shows. Do not paste this into product descriptions or theme.liquid.
target_ui_hint: Online Store > Themes > Customize > Products > Default product
